_comment: The shape of GET /api/companion/status that Cubie's bridge consumes.
Not documentation: scripts/check_companion_contract.py compares this against
Virtual-Office's server/src/companion/companionStatus.ts and fails on drift.
The bridge maps these fields onto device MCP calls (posture, LEDs, screen), so
a rename upstream is a totem that quietly stops reflecting the office.
notes: present is ABSENT when unknown, false when the desk is known empty. Cubie must
not collapse them: absent means fall back to the office's own routing.
pendingTotal and founderTasksTotal may exceed their list lengths -- the lists
are capped. Showing a short list as if it were everything is the failure those
blocked and review are different actions, not shades of one: blocked means a
team asked a question and cannot continue; review means work is delivered and
waiting to be accepted. Cubie must say which, or it sends its owner to do
ts is epoch MILLISECONDS (~1.8e12), so it needs 64 bits. This bit the K10:
`long` is 32-bit on an ESP32 and 64-bit on a test host, so strtol saturated on
the device while every host test passed.
mood is decided server-side. Deriving it on-device would be a second
definition of 'busy', free to disagree with the wall.

nowPlaying is ABSENT for many different reasons at once -- the office has no Spotify, nothing is playing, it is paused, an ad is on with no track attached, or Spotify could not be reached. They all mean the same thing to a robot: there is nothing to dance to. The office separates them in its own log.

inTheRoom is SERVED, not filtered on. Music on headphones or on a phone elsewhere is still playing, and a wall display showing the track has every reason to want it. Cubie is the one that must not dance to false -- a robot dancing to a silent room is a bug that looks like charm, so nobody reports it.
